blocks.value: Recursion is the first idea in this course that feels like a trick. A method that calls itself sounds circular, like a definition that never resolves.

It resolves because each call works on a **smaller** problem, and because there is always a case small enough to answer outright. Once that clicks, a class of problems, trees, nested structures, divide and conquer, becomes dramatically easier to write than with loops.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Define recursion and identify a recursive method
Distinguish the base case from the general case
Trace the execution of a recursive call
Design a recursive solution to a problem
Compare recursion with iteration and choose between them
